# mergewf_user_tool_access_policy (Resource)

Manages the complete user tool access policy, including all rules. Import using the subject ID. Removing a group/user policy restores inherited access.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "mergewf_user_tool_access_policy" "example" {
  user_id = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
  mode    = "CUSTOM"
  rules   = [{ action = "ALLOW", connector = "github", tool_class = "READ_ONLY" }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mode` (String) API field `mode`. Allowed values: `ALL`, `CUSTOM`, `NONE`.
- `user_id` (String) API field `user_id`. Minimum length: 1.

### Optional

- `rules` (Attributes List) API field `rules`. Omit to accept the server value; use an explicit empty collection to clear a collection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Terraform resource identity. See the resource description for its import format.
- `result_json` (String) Complete API response encoded as JSON. Use jsondecode to access additional response fields. Stored in Terraform state.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) action. Allowed values: `ALLOW`, `DENY`.

Optional:

- `connector` (String) connector. Minimum length: 1. Maximum length: 100.
- `tool` (String) tool. Minimum length: 1. Maximum length: 200.
- `tool_class` (String) tool_class. Allowed values: `READ_ONLY`, `WRITE`, `DESTRUCTIVE`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import mergewf_user_tool_access_policy.example USER_ID
```
